Held by a subtype: no · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/GangOfFour/Memento.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage/GangOfFour/MementoUsage.cs)

### Observer (Gang of Four)

Defines a one to many dependency between objects, so that when one object changes state all its dependents are notified and updated automatically.

*Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides, Design Patterns, 1994.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Subject | `[Observer.Subject]` | interface, class | yes | `Observer` |
| ConcreteSubject | `[Observer.ConcreteSubject]` | class | yes | `Subject` |
| Observer | `[Observer.Observer]` | interface, class | yes | — |
| ConcreteObserver | `[Observer.ConcreteObserver]` | class | yes | `Observer`, `ConcreteSubject` |
| NotifyMethod | `[Observer.NotifyMethod]` | method | no | — |
| UpdateMethod | `[Observer.UpdateMethod]` | method | no | — |

**Subject** — Knows its observers, and declares the operations to attach and detach them.

**ConcreteSubject** — Holds the state of interest, and notifies its observers when it changes.

**Observer** — Declares the update operation invoked when the observed subject changes.

**ConcreteObserver** — Reacts to the notification, and keeps itself consistent with the subject.

**NotifyMethod** — The operation that informs every registered observer of a change.

**UpdateMethod** — The operation invoked on an observer when the subject has changed.

Held by a subtype: no · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/GangOfFour/Observer.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage/GangOfFour/ObserverUsage.cs)

### Prototype (Gang of Four)

Specifies the kinds of objects to create using a prototypical instance, and creates new objects by copying that prototype.

*Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides, Design Patterns, 1994.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Prototype | `[Prototype.Prototype]` | interface, class | yes | — |
| ConcretePrototype | `[Prototype.ConcretePrototype]` | class, struct | yes | `Prototype` |
| CloneMethod | `[Prototype.CloneMethod]` | method | no | — |

**Prototype** — Declares the operation that clones itself.

**ConcretePrototype** — Implements the cloning operation for its own representation.

**CloneMethod** — The operation that returns a copy of the prototype.

Held by a subtype: no · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/GangOfFour/Prototype.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage/GangOfFour/PrototypeUsage.cs)

### Proxy (Gang of Four)

Provides a surrogate or placeholder for another object in order to control access to it.

*Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides, Design Patterns, 1994.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Subject | `[Proxy.Subject]` | interface, class | yes | — |
| RealSubject | `[Proxy.RealSubject]` | class | yes | `Subject` |
| Proxy | `[Proxy.Proxy]` | class | yes | `Subject`, `RealSubject` |

**Subject** — Declares the interface shared by the real object and its proxy, so that they are interchangeable.

**RealSubject** — The object the proxy stands for, and which does the real work.

**Proxy** — Controls access to the real subject, and may be responsible for creating it.

Ensures a type has only one instance, and provides a global point of access to it.

*Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides, Design Patterns, 1994.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |

| Singleton | `[Singleton]` | class | no | — |

### State (Gang of Four)

Lets an object alter its behaviour when its internal state changes, so that it appears to change its class.

*Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides, Design Patterns, 1994.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |

**State** — Declares the behaviour that varies with the state of the context.

**ConcreteState** — Implements the behaviour associated with one state of the context.

### Strategy (Gang of Four)

Defines a family of interchangeable algorithms, encapsulates each one, and lets the algorithm vary independently from the clients that use it.

*Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides, Design Patterns, 1994.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |

| Context | `[Strategy.Context]` | class | yes | `Strategy` |
| Strategy | `[Strategy.Strategy]` | interface, class | yes | — |
| ConcreteStrategy | `[Strategy.ConcreteStrategy]` | class, struct | yes | `Strategy` |

**Context** — Is configured with a strategy, and delegates the algorithm to it.

**Strategy** — Declares the interface common to every supported algorithm.

**ConcreteStrategy** — Implements one algorithm behind the strategy interface.

### TemplateMethod (Gang of Four)

Defines the skeleton of an algorithm in an operation, deferring some steps to subclasses so they can redefine them without changing the algorithm's structure.

*Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides, Design Patterns, 1994.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AbstractClass | `[TemplateMethod.AbstractClass]` | class | yes | — |
| ConcreteClass | `[TemplateMethod.ConcreteClass]` | class | yes | `AbstractClass` |
| TemplateMethod | `[TemplateMethod.TemplateMethod]` | method | no | — |
| PrimitiveOperation | `[TemplateMethod.PrimitiveOperation]` | method | no | — |
| HookOperation | `[TemplateMethod.HookOperation]` | method | no | — |

**AbstractClass** — Defines the skeleton of the algorithm, and declares the steps subclasses must supply.

**ConcreteClass** — Supplies the steps the algorithm defers to subclasses.

**TemplateMethod** — The operation that holds the skeleton of the algorithm, and calls the deferred steps.

**PrimitiveOperation** — A step the algorithm defers, and which subclasses must supply.

**HookOperation** — A step the algorithm defers, and which subclasses may override, but need not.

Held by a subtype: no · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/GangOfFour/TemplateMethod.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage/GangOfFour/TemplateMethodUsage.cs)

### Visitor (Gang of Four)

Represents an operation to be performed on the elements of an object structure, and lets a new operation be defined without changing the classes of those elements.

*Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides, Design Patterns, 1994.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Visitor | `[Visitor.Visitor]` | interface, class | yes | — |
| ConcreteVisitor | `[Visitor.ConcreteVisitor]` | class | yes | `Visitor` |
| Element | `[Visitor.Element]` | interface, class | yes | — |
| ConcreteElement | `[Visitor.ConcreteElement]` | class, struct | yes | `Element` |
| ObjectStructure | `[Visitor.ObjectStructure]` | class | yes | `Element` |
| VisitMethod | `[Visitor.VisitMethod]` | method | no | `ConcreteElement` |
| AcceptMethod | `[Visitor.AcceptMethod]` | method | no | — |

**Visitor** — Declares one visit operation per concrete element of the structure.

**ConcreteVisitor** — Implements the visit operations: this is where the added algorithm lives.

**Element** — Declares the entry point of the double dispatch.

**ConcreteElement** — Dispatches to the visit operation that corresponds to its own type.

**ObjectStructure** — Holds the elements, and offers a way to walk them.

**VisitMethod** — The operation applied to one given concrete element.

**AcceptMethod** — The entry point of the double dispatch: it calls back the matching visit operation.

Held by a subtype: no · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/GangOfFour/Visitor.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage/GangOfFour/VisitorUsage.cs)


## no catalog of its own

`Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Idioms` — 2 patterns, 2 roles.

### NullObject (no catalog of its own)

A special case whose behaviour is to do nothing, so that the absence of a collaborator needs no null check.

*Bobby Woolf, Pattern Languages of Program Design 3, 1997.*

A narrower case of **SpecialCase** (Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture): every participant here is one of those too.

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NullObject | `[NullObject]` | class, struct | no | — |

**NullObject** — The do-nothing member of a protocol. It is a special case narrowed to one behaviour — neutral: its queries answer the identity of whatever the caller does with them, and its commands are accepted and ignored. A special case that answers something meaningful, such as an unknown customer with a default rate, is not one of these.

Held by a subtype: yes · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/Idioms/NullObject.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage/Idioms/NullObjectUsage.cs)

### ObjectMother (no catalog of its own)

A class that builds fully formed objects for tests, so that a test states what matters about its data and nothing else.

*Peter Schuh and Stephanie Punke, ObjectMother: Easing Test Object Creation in XP (XP Universe), 2001.*

| Role | Annotation | Applies to | Repeatable | Links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ObjectMother | `[ObjectMother]` | class | no | — |

**ObjectMother** — The source of test objects. Each of its methods returns an object already valid and already meaningful — a lapsed subscription, an overdrawn account — named for the SITUATION rather than for the shape, which is what keeps the intent of a test in the test rather than in twenty lines of construction.

Held by a subtype: no · [Source](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes/Idioms/ObjectMother.cs) · [Sample](../../Reefact.LivingDocumentation.Attributes.Usage/Idioms/ObjectMotherUsage.cs)
